parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Haemoglobin is made of two $\alpha$-globin chains and two $\beta$-globin chains.

A person may have a mutation in the gene coding for $\beta$-globin. This is due to a base substitution and leads to the production of abnormal $\beta$-globin and therefore abnormal haemoglobin.

A person who is homozygous for the mutant allele will have a condition called sickle cell anaemia.

Outline the phenotypic effects of having abnormal haemoglobin in a person with sickle cell anaemia.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
$Hb^A$ is the allele coding for normal $\beta$-globin.

$Hb^S$ is the allele coding for abnormal $\beta$-globin.

The alleles are codominant.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by the alleles being codominant.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
A person who is heterozygous will have sickle cell trait but may not experience the symptoms of sickle cell anaemia.

Suggest why a person with sickle cell trait may not show the symptoms of sickle cell anaemia.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
Construct a genetic diagram to show the possible offspring for a man and a woman who both have sickle cell trait.
